screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a particle detector seen along the beam: the tracker at the centre, then the electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters, the solenoid, and the muon chambers. A collision event shows curved tracks, calorimeter deposits, muon hits and a missing-momentum arrow.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose Explore or the What was this? game, pick a collision type, make new events, change the magnetic field, and measure a selected track's curvature.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Select a track to read its radius and momentum, then switch the field down and watch the tracks curl.

eventDisplay.currentDetailsPattern: Event with {{tracks}} tracks and {{deposits}} calorimeter deposits; missing transverse momentum {{missing}} GeV.

controls.bank: Add this decay to the lifetime estimate

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a histogram of the invariant mass of muon pairs recorded by the CMS detector in 2011. Peaks mark particles that decayed into two muons.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose how the histogram is filled, one pair at a time, as a stream, or all at once, and switch between the full spectrum and the Z region. A fit panel measures the Z boson's mass, width and lifetime.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Add a few pairs by hand, then stream events and watch the peaks appear.

controls.add: Add this pair to the histogram

screenSummary.playArea: A log–log graph of the collision energy √s against beam energy, for a fixed target and for a collider, with production thresholds and historic machines marked.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose proton or electron beams and set the beam energy. Readouts compare the two configurations and list what each can make.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Slide the beam energy up and compare how fast the two curves rise.
